title: Auditable Carbon Credit Ledger
business: Environmental compliance firms managing carbon credit issuance and trading.
problem: Traditional CRUD databases overwrite current state, losing the historical context required for regulatory audits and preventing the reconstruction of credit balances at specific past timestamps.
solution: Event Sourcing stores an append-only sequence of domain events as the authoritative state history, allowing the system to derive the current balance by replaying the event stream from the beginning.
steps: Define immutable event types such as CreditIssued, CreditTransferred, and CreditRetired.
Append each new event to an immutable event store instead of updating a current balance row.
Implement a projection engine that consumes the event stream to build a read-optimized view of current balances.
Use the event stream to reconstruct the state of any account at any point in time for audit verification.
outcome: The system gains a complete, immutable audit trail of every credit movement, ensuring regulatory compliance and enabling point-in-time state reconstruction.
limitation: The primary limitation is the complexity of evolving the event schema over time; to check for this, monitor the cost of migration scripts required to handle legacy event formats when business rules change.

questions.question: In Auditable Carbon Credit Ledger, why is Event Sourcing used instead of a standard database update?
options: To enable point-in-time state reconstruction and auditability.
To improve the performance of simple read queries.
To reduce the total number of database tables required.
To eliminate the need for a service layer.
questions.explanation: Event Sourcing preserves the history of changes, which is necessary for the audit requirements described in the scenario.
questions.evidence: Traditional CRUD databases overwrite current state, losing the historical context required for regulatory audits and preventing the reconstruction of credit balances at specific past timestamps.

questions.question: What is a key trade-off when implementing Event Sourcing in Auditable Carbon Credit Ledger?
options: The system becomes impossible to scale horizontally.
The difficulty of managing schema evolution over time.
The loss of data integrity during event replays.
The requirement to use only relational databases.
questions.explanation: As noted in the limitations, evolving the event schema is a significant challenge in event-sourced systems.
questions.evidence: The primary limitation is the complexity of evolving the event schema over time; to check for this, monitor the cost of migration scripts required to handle legacy event formats when business rules change.
